New Delhi, Nov 14 (ANI): Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta poses for a picture during her visit to the Delhi Pavilion at the India International Trade Fair (ITTF) at Bharat Mandapam, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI Photo/ Shagun Chauhan) | Photo Credit: ANI
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday inaugurated the Delhi Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF-2026), being held at Bharat Mandapam.
Delhi has been designated the Focus State at this year’s fair. Ms. Gupta said the opportunity was being used to showcase the Capital’s growing economic, cultural and industrial identity.
“The Delhi Pavilion brings together the Capital’s glorious heritage and its journey of modern development. It also provides entrepreneurs, women business owners, artisans and local producers with an opportunity to showcase their talent and products and gain wider recognition,” she said.
She added that the Delhi government aimed to preserve the Capital’s cultural identity while highlighting its work in development, innovation, entrepreneurship and environmental conservation at national and international levels.
Spread over 996 sq. metres, the pavilion features 62 stalls, 10 of which have been allocated to women entrepreneurs.
According to a Delhi government statement, the pavilion showcases the city’s art, culture, historical identity and heritage, along with initiatives such as Namo Van, Swachh Yamuna and the promotion of electric vehicles.
“Through these displays, visitors will get to know about the development works underway in Delhi, the efforts being made towards environmental conservation and the Capital’s future development priorities,” the statement said.
After visiting the stalls and interacting with participants, Ms. Gupta said Delhi was not only the national Capital but also a symbol of India’s rich historical heritage, diverse culture, entrepreneurship and modern development.
“Through the Delhi Pavilion, this multifaceted identity of the Capital is being showcased on national and international platforms,” she said.
IITF 2026 will run from November 13 to 27 across 17 halls at Bharat Mandapam under the theme ‘Vikas aur Virasat’. Business-only days will continue until November 18.
The fair has brought together more than 3,500 exhibitors from India and abroad across over 1 lakh sq. metres of exhibition space. It will see participation from 32 States and Union Territories and 51 Central Ministries, government departments, public sector undertakings and public sector banks.
International participation includes 11 countries, with pavilions featuring exhibitors from Thailand, Iran, Ghana, Nepal, Afghanistan, the UAE, Turkey, China, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, providing opportunities for business engagement and trade linkages.
